identity.title: ALMAGAL: V. Relations between the core populations and the parent clump physical properties

paper_type_evidence.quote: A major step toward a statistical approach to clump fragmentation, covering a large variety of physical conditions and Galactic locations, is represented by ALMAGAL (ALMA Cycle 7 large project

targets.name: 1007 ALMAGAL clumps in the Galactic plane (Hi-GAL and RMS selected)

redshift_or_distance.value: heliocentric distances, mostly ~2-8 kpc; near d <= 4.66 kpc and far d > 4.66 kpc

evidence.quote: Of the 1017 targets initially present in the ALMAGAL observing plan, 1007 are analyzed in this work.

distance_source.value: Megeath/Mege et al. (cite: meg21), updated by Benedettini et al. (in prep.) using ALMAGAL line radial velocities

evidence.quote: Of the 1017 targets initially present in the ALMAGAL observing plan, 1007 are analyzed in this work.

question.value: How do the number, mass and formation efficiency of cores in ALMAGAL clumps correlate with the clump physical parameters and evolutionary indicators, and which star formation scenario (core-fed or clump-fed) do they favour?

evidence.quote: This study aims at correlating the fragmentation properties of massive clumps, obtained from ALMA observations, with their global physical parameters
as observed in continuum maps at 1.4 mm of the ALMAGAL survey
the compact configurations C-2 and C-3 (collectively referred to as TM2), and the extended configurations C-5 and C-6 (summarized as TM1) were combined with data from the 7m array

configurations.value: near (d<=4.66 kpc): C2+C5, 476 targets; far (d>4.66 kpc): C3+C6, 531 targets

evidence.quote: the “near” distance for $d \leq 4.66$ kpc (C2+C5 configurations, 476 targets observed), and the “far” distance for $d > 4.66$ kpc (C3+C6 configurations, 531 targets observed)

sensitivity.value: 90% flux completeness 0.95 mJy (0.13 and 0.37 Msun at d=3.5 and 6 kpc)

evidence.quote: The 90% flux completeness in the catalog is 0.95 mJy, which translates into 0.13 and 0.37 M$_\odot$ at $d=3.5$ and 6 kpc, respectively.

provided.value: 70-500 micron clump photometry, SED fits, masses, temperatures, luminosities

evidence.quote: For these 1007 objects, physical properties are calculated from Hi-GAL photometry

provided.value: radio counterparts to identify UCHII regions

evidence.quote: we searched for possible compact or ultra-compact HII (UCHII) region counterparts in the source catalogs of the radio surveys CORNISH (cite: pur13) and CORNISH South (cite: ira23)

what.value: Core catalog (positions, flux densities, masses) extracted from ALMAGAL 7M+TM2+TM1 continuum maps

evidence.quote: The morphologic, photometric, and physical properties of fragments detected in ALMAGAL continuum observations were determined by (cite: col25).

what.value: Clump physical parameters (mass, T, L, Tbol) from Hi-GAL catalogs

evidence.quote: For the subsample of sources selected directly from the Hi-GAL catalog, data are taken from (cite: eli21).

what.value: Updated rescaled distance-dependent clump quantities and RMS-target recovery

evidence.quote: Hence, re-scaled distance-dependent quantities were listed by (cite: mol25).

what.value: Sink particle number and mass vs L/M from Rosetta Stone simulations

evidence.quote: We use recent numerical simulations produced by the Rosetta Stone project (cite: leb25)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Rosetta Stone RAMSES magnetized collapse of a 500 Msun clump (Mach 7, mu=10, T=10 K, ~0.38 pc), sink particles above 1e9 cm-3, ~400 au resolution

evidence.quote: initial clump size $\sim 0.38$ pc (total size of the cube $\sim 1.5$ pc), mass $M=500~M_\odot$, turbulent Mach number $\mathcal{M}=7$
the final products considered by (cite: col25) are called 7M+TM2+TM1 maps.

what.value: Core detection and photometry with CuTEx adapted to ALMAGAL maps

evidence.quote: The fragment[^2] detection and photometry in the ALMAGAL fields were carried out with the CuTEx algorithm (cite: mol11), specifically adapted to the ALMAGAL maps, as detailed in (cite: col25).

what.value: Core flux to mass conversion with kappa=0.9 cm2/g at 1.3 mm and temperature scheme by clump L/M

evidence.quote: assuming an opacity of 0.9 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 1.3 mm, suitable for dense environments (cite: oss94; san19), a gas-to-dust ratio of 100

what.value: Clump SED fitting and bolometric temperature estimate

evidence.quote: estimated as described in (cite: eli17)

unstated_but_needed: Exact formula and normalization of Tcore ∝ (L/M)^0.22 for L/M>10
Binning scheme (bin edges) for the median trends
Fitting procedure details for power laws (weights, log space, data selection)
Final ALMAGAL core catalog contents and version needed (from Coletta et al.)
Exact clump catalog values after distance update (Benedettini et al. in prep.)
Simulation sink curve data used in the figures

method.value: Combine Hi-GAL clump parameters with ALMAGAL core catalog; classify as quiescent, star-forming, UCHII (CORNISH match within 10 arcsec)

evidence.quote: Adopting a searching radius of 10$''$, 24 and 50 matches with ALMAGAL were found in the former and the latter, respectively.

assumptions.value: Clump kappa300=10 cm2/g, beta=2, gas-to-dust 100; non-deconvolved sizes for surface density

evidence.quote: A modified black body (cite: eli16) with a mass opacity coefficient (hereafter opacity) of $\kappa_{300}=10$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 300 $\mu$m

method.value: Compute Ncore, mass of most massive core MMC, fMMC and CFE = total core mass / clump mass

evidence.quote: defined as the total mass of the cores identified in a clump divided by the clump’s total mass

validation.value: Checked distance bias; restricted to 2<d<6 kpc; free-free-free subsample in Appendix

evidence.quote: we recalculated all median trends of the other clump parameters shown in panels $b$ to $f$ of Figure [7](#massmaxvsall) by considering only targets located at $2~\mathrm{kpc} < d < 6~\mathrm{kpc}$.

method.value: Medians in bins, Spearman matrix, two-sample K-S test between classes, power-law least-squares fits

evidence.quote: we obtain coefficients $\rho_\mathrm{S}$ by considering the $n=840$ ALMAGAL targets with all clump properties defined and $N_\mathrm{core} \geq 1$.

fitting.value: Power laws by least squares; uncertainties from the fit

evidence.quote: (parameter uncertainties are simply derived from least squares fitting to data)

validation.value: Resampling of 100 subsamples of 30 points; critical Spearman values from Student t

evidence.quote: we performed a resampling test by extracting 100 random subsamples of 30 data points (out of 840) for each pair of variables

method.value: Overplot Rosetta Stone sink count, sink efficiency and max sink mass vs L/M and compare with core-fed and clump-fed predictions

evidence.quote: The predicted number of sink particles (gray line in Figure [17](#ncoremultiplot), and orange in Figure [4](#ncoresvsall) (panel $d$)) exceeds most ALMAGAL values by a factor $\gtrsim 2$

used_for.value: core detection and photometry in ALMAGAL maps (done in Coletta et al.)

evidence.quote: carried out with the CuTEx algorithm (cite: mol11)
by using the RAMSES code (cite: tey02; fro06)
The ALMAGAL sample is divided in 891 star-forming and 116 quiescent sources, respectively.

results_numeric.quantity: Spearman rho Mmmc vs clump mass

evidence.quote: A large scatter is found, with a Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient $\rho_\mathrm{S}=0.34$.
the best-fit exponent is found to be $0.75\pm 0.06$ for the entire population
\mathrm{CFE}=10^{-2.54\pm 0.02}\;\left[\frac{L/M}{\mathrm{L}_\odot/\mathrm{M}_\odot}\right]^{0.36\pm 0.02}
\mathrm{CFE}=10^{-5.42\pm 0.13}\;\left[\frac{T}{\mathrm{K}}\right]^{2.5\pm 0.1}
the derived CFEs range from 0.01% to 15%, with a median of 0.4%
Looking in particular at the 31 clumps with $M_\mathrm{MMC} > 24~\mathrm{M}_\odot$

results_numeric.quantity: K-S statistic Ncore quiescent vs star-forming

evidence.quote: In this case, the K-S statistic is $D=0.31$

findings_qualitative.value: Ncore correlates preferentially with clump surface density, not with total clump mass

evidence.quote: The fragmentation level correlates preferentially with clump surface density, supporting a scenario of density-driven fragmentation

findings_qualitative.value: Cores above 24 Msun are absent in quiescent clumps and found only in clumps with Sigma > 0.3 g cm-2

evidence.quote: Cores with masses of at least 24 M$_\odot$ (i.e., three times the 8 M$_\odot$ threshold for defining a massive star) are exclusively found in clumps with a surface density exceeding 0.3 g cm$^{-2}$

claims.hypothesis: Fragmentation level depends on clump mass or surface density
claims.experiment: Ncore vs M and Sigma, medians and Spearman
claims.result: No clear dependence on M; clearer increase with Sigma

evidence.quote: whereas it does not show any clear dependence on total clump mass

claims.hypothesis: Core growth continues during clump evolution
claims.experiment: MMC and CFE vs T, L/M
claims.result: Both increase on average by an order of magnitude with large scatter

evidence.quote: This suggests that core growth continues throughout the clump evolution, favoring clump-fed over core-fed theoretical scenarios.

claims.experiment: Compare Rosetta Stone 500 Msun mu=10 sinks with Ncore and CFE
claims.result: Similar trends but simulations exceed observations by factor >=2
claims.finding: Stellar feedback, sensitivity and resolution may explain the discrepancy

evidence.quote: Stellar feedback, not yet included in these simulations, can contribute to suppress fragmentation

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Core-fed model rejected because core masses and CFE increase with time and no isolated massive cores are seen

evidence.quote: multiple arguments emerge against a core-fed scenario

limitations_admitted.value: Continuum data cannot quantify magnetic fields, turbulence or feedback; Ncore values may be lower limits due to sensitivity

evidence.quote: the $N_\mathrm{core}$ values plotted in various figures might be intended as lower limits for this quantity.

referee_caveats_inferred: Core masses assume temperatures from clump L/M, so trends with L/M may be partly built in
Clump and core opacities differ by a factor 1.7, affecting CFE
Spearman significance is ambiguous at n=840
Ncore is sensitivity limited and distance dependent

Simulation outputs from Lebreuilly et al.

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Depends on unreleased or companion catalogs and unspecified binning; project code not printed.
